title: Branch drift, drawn two ways
question: Does the diagram let a reader say whether the branch merges cleanly?

verdicts.label: Drop
verdicts.gloss: the diagram does not answer the brief

blocks.label: Brief
blocks.text: Draw how far a branch has drifted from main: the commits on each side since they parted, and the files both sides touched. A reader should see at a glance whether the branch still merges cleanly.

blocks.label: Method
blocks.text: Lay both lines on one time axis and mark the fork, then count commits on each side.

outputs.title: Two lines from a fork
outputs.text: Main and the branch leave the fork together; main has moved four commits, the branch two. The overlap file is named under the gap, so the risk sits where the eye lands.

outputs.title: Age bar
outputs.text: One bar for the time since the fork, split by who moved. It reads faster than the lines but drops which files overlap, so it cannot answer the brief alone.
outputs.sketch: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 140" font-family="Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif"><rect width="480" height="140" fill="#ffffff"/><text x="20" y="36" font-size="18" fill="#334155">9 days since the fork</text><rect x="20" y="56" width="290" height="36" fill="#334155"/><rect x="310" y="56" width="150" height="36" fill="#2563eb"/><text x="30" y="80" font-size="16" fill="#ffffff">main: 4 commits</text><text x="318" y="80" font-size="16" fill="#ffffff">branch: 2</text><text x="20" y="122" font-size="15" fill="#64748b">overlap not shown</text></svg>

blocks.label: Method
blocks.text: Start from the files, not the commits: one row per file either side touched, one column per side.

outputs.title: Files by side
outputs.text: Each file is a row and each side a column; a row filled on both sides is the conflict risk, tinted red. The commit counts sit in the column heads.

outputs.text: The matrix reduced to one sentence, drawn as an HTML fragment rather than an image, to show the page draws both kinds.
